precepts.text: The Lord said, where two or three gather, I'm in the midst of you. We don't see that.
precepts.point: Right? The Lord showed him something that nobody could see. Open his eyes, and he could see what's behind him. In the spiritual realm, there's angels all around us. The Lord said, where two or three gather, I'm in the midst of you. We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident. And there will come a time where some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears and show us and direct our path, and reveal to us things that the world... And I have some images on that too, if you look in there, angels in the heavens, that will reveal those things. But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. Again, if you still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. You're not going to be able to have foresight. A part of that is also having foresight, revealing these things. Read that verse again, and we going to move on.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Elisha prayed, “Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see”, and the young man saw “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.” The Lord showed him something nobody could see: he opened his eyes, and he could see what was behind him. In the spiritual realm, there are angels all around us.

The Lord said it: “where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” We don't see that. But the Lord will open up his spirit to make it evident, the way he opened the young man's eyes.

There will come a time when some of us will see things, and God will whisper in our ears, show us, direct our path and reveal things to us. That is one of the spiritual senses being activated, and part of it is having foresight.

But you have to move from milk to meat to tap into that. If you are still caught up in your old sins, you ain't going to be able to see these things. The Lord is in the midst of his people when they gather in his name; it is the ones who have come out of their sins whose eyes he opens to see it.

precepts.text: It were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
precepts.point: Apollonius, pretending peace, forbare till the holy day of the Sabbath, and taking the Jews keeping holy day, commanded his men to arm themselves, and slew all them that were gone to the celebrating of the Sabbath. But Judas Maccabeus with nine others withdrew himself into the wilderness, and lived in the mountains after the manner of beasts, and fed on herbs continually, lest they should be partakers of the pollution.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
When a false rumour went out that Antiochus was dead, Jason took a thousand men and assaulted the city. “But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen.” He despised his own people.

“Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason.” You think you can be a traitor and be honored and respected? No. Nobody likes a traitor. Even in Rise of the Planet of the Apes, the whole movie is about black people, they spray painted the word donkey on the traitor apes. That is the brothers who were in here in 2018, and some of the brothers who just bugged out in LA. You cannot be trusted.

Christ spoke of what it is to harm his own: “But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.” It would be better for the betrayer to have a millstone hanged about his neck and be drowned.

Jason offended and slew those who belonged to the Lord, and he got his reward: shame, fleeing from city to city, and dying in a strange land.

precepts.text: If thy brother trespass against thee, go tell him his fault between thee and him alone; then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established; and if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican. This is for major things, not petty complaints. Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not deal with them, and the heathen were the other nations. Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you, and they always keep a little way back into your life, with fair speeches and kind words, to win you over to Satan.
precepts.point: On family: we do not break up families. If your family does not have an issue with you being in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
When we are warned not to be beguiled, and to avoid them that cause division, it is so that you and I don't get seduced: but he or she was my friend, I think I can win them back. No. Stop it. Christ laid out the order: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.”

“But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.” This is for major things. It's not about stupidity like somebody moving your pencil from the right side of the table to the left, or a sister wanting people thrown out of the school because nobody likes her unleavened bread. You can't cook? Learn. We aren't throwing anybody out over your bread.

“And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” Publicans were tax collectors; the Israelites did not like them and did not talk with them. The heathen were the other nations. So deal with him like that. You don't know better than Christ.

Christ is warning you to separate from them, because they will seduce you. They always keep a little way to get back into your life, a little hot pocket, to win you over to Satan with fair speeches and kind words: I always liked you, you were my favorite deacon, come over for dinner tonight, you're different than the rest of them. All that is to seduce you.

precepts.text: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him. And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him. That brother is the children of thy people, per Leviticus 19:17.
precepts.point: Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ's seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance, the perpetual hatred Esau carries against his brother Jacob. Now the flip side: Peter asked, “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” Christ answered, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Christ offers boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to do the same.

Luke gives the terms: “Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.” That brother is the children of thy people, as Leviticus 19:17 says. It is rebuke first, then repentance, then forgiveness.

“And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.” Why? Seven represents completion. The same way Christ forgave us when we were without sacrifice and without mercy: all our adulteries, fornication, lying and stealing during Assyria, Babylon, Persia and America, scattered in Africa in the dark ages doing all sorts of wicked things. Christ forgave all of that. That is why he said seventy times seven.

precepts.text: Put on therefore, as the elect of God, bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, even as Christ forgave you. Some of us hold grudges like there is no tomorrow; imagine if Christ held on to grudges toward us. We would not be here. Forgiveness is something to pray for.
precepts.point: Lamech's seventy and sevenfold was complete vengeance; Christ's seventy times seven is complete, boundless, endless mercy to the Israelites who believe, and he told Peter to extend the same.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved, bowels of mercies, kindness”, the mercy Christ offers us, “humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering”: longsuffering toward the brother who repents. “Forbearing one another”, as Christ forbears us, “and forgiving one another”.

Forgiving is something some of us need to pray for. Some can forgive nothing and hold on to grudges like there is no tomorrow. Imagine if Christ held on to grudges against us. We would not be here; we would be in hell with white Jesus, Islam and our sins. The only reason we are here is Jesus Christ and his boundless mercy toward us.

“If any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” Christ does not put numbers out just to put them. Seventy times seven is 490, and Daniel's seventy weeks, 490 years from Persia to Christ, were determined “to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity” through the Messiah cut off for the children of Israel. We could not sacrifice in Babylon and Persia; we needed Christ, the complete perfection of mercy. He forgave us seventy times seven, so we forgive our brother the same, and we do not take him for granted.

precepts.text: The preparations of the heart in man and the answer of the tongue are from the Lord: even your coming to the leadership table you want to fight was ordained before time, and the Lord seals a man's instruction in his sleep.
precepts.point: Your issue is not with leadership; you are bitter towards the Lord.

note.label: Eleutherophobia the Fear of Freedom

precepts.why:
Christ told the twelve, “Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven”. Someone thinks it's just leadership saying it. No: “The preparations of the heart in man, and the answer of the tongue, is from the Lord.” The Lord had already ordained you to come up to that leadership table. Even your walking up to the council you want to go against was declared before time, as Isaiah 46:10 says, declaring the end from the beginning. God already agreed.

The preparing of your mind is from the Lord. You may say, I'm going to get up at 9:00 today and make it to the gym. The Lord says no, you are getting up at 10:00, and you'll get out the bed on the left-hand side and stub your damn toe. You set that timer to the T all week, you're a light sleeper, and that joker doesn't ring, because that was the Lord's doing. The Lord seals man's instruction in his sleep.

And the answer of the tongue, is that from the man or the woman? It is from the Lord. The Lord dictates even what you are going to respond back. The Lord may send a spirit down on you to go contrary to the doctrine, contrary to what leadership says in counsel to save your life, and you don't even catch that it is a spirit speaking through you. That is also a learning experience, for you to catch yourself.

But many cannot shake that legion. They ride that wave onto the bitterness boat and find themselves outside the congregation, making three- and four-part emotional videos and complaining on Clubhouse about how they were done unjustly. Then the Lord blinds your mind; you are reprobate, and only if the Lord chooses will he bring you back.

So your issue is not with leadership; you are bitter toward the Lord. Leadership has nothing to gain by telling you the word. All we gave you was the word of God, and we will be judged for it. Take it here and forbear, or go out there and get burnt. Our people hate their freedom; they are fearful of freedom, of responsibility, and of leadership.

precepts.text: Not until seven times, but until seventy times seven; the law of forgiveness Joseph showed his brethren.
precepts.point: The famine itself was called by the Most High, and the man was sent before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant, whose feet they hurt with fetters. The fetters and the iron are the prison where the king's prisoners were bound.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
Peter asked, “Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” and Christ answered, “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” That is the law of forgiveness, and Joseph kept it. His own brothers sold him into slavery, and he told them, “be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.”

That is the law Israel must keep with one another today: forgive thy brother, not until seven times, but until seventy times seven.

precepts.text: Where two or three are gathered together in his name, there he is in the midst of them; the presence in the midst is the separation from the nations.
precepts.point: The presence of the Most High in the midst is how Israel is known to be separated from all the nations, and it ties back to the sabbath sign: when Israel keeps the sabbath and gathers in his name, the Lord and Christ are in the midst.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

precepts.why:
Moses said, “If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence. For wherein shall it be known here that I and thy people have found grace in thy sight? is it not in that thou goest with us? so shall we be separated, I and thy people, from all the people that are upon the face of the earth.” The presence of the Most High in the midst is how Israel is known to be separated from all the nations.

Christ says, “For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.” It ties back to the sabbath sign: when Israel keeps the sabbath and gathers in his name, the Lord and Christ are in the midst, and that presence is still the separation from all the people upon the face of the earth.

precepts.text: Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: Stay humble with it: Lord, my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty; neither do I exercise myself in great matters, or in things too high for me; David behaved and quieted himself as a child that is weaned of his mother. Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven; so behave yourselves humbly, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
The disciples asked who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven, and Christ called a little child and set him in the midst of them: “Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

So behave yourselves humbly, as newborn babes desiring the milk of the word, as a child weaned of his mother, and the Most High will establish thine heart and increase thy wisdom.

precepts.text: Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven; Moses' intercession loosed the judgment, and the Lord pardoned according to his word.
precepts.point: Moses interceded: the Egyptians and the nations would hear that the Lord was not able to bring the people into the land and slew them in the wilderness. He pleaded, Let the power of my Lord be great, the Lord is longsuffering and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity; pardon this people according to the greatness of thy mercy, as thou hast forgiven them from Egypt until now. This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed.

note.label: Numbers 14: The Congregation Rebels and Is Condemned

precepts.why:
The Lord said He would smite the people with the pestilence and disinherit them and make of Moses a greater nation. Moses interceded instead: the Egyptians and the nations would say “Because the Lord was not able to bring this people into the land which he sware unto them, therefore he hath slain them in the wilderness.” He pleaded, “let the power of my Lord be great”, “The Lord is longsuffering, and of great mercy, forgiving iniquity and transgression”, and “Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”

“Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.” Moses' intercession loosed the judgment on earth, and the Lord pardoned according to his word.

This is a true leader interceding for the people rather than seeing them destroyed, and what the man of God loosed on earth was loosed in heaven.

precepts.text: If thy brother trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault alone; if he will not hear, take one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established, and then tell it unto the church.
precepts.point: These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.” If your brother trespasses against you, you do not go and shoot, stab, or fight him; you speak to him alone. “But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established”, the same two or three witnesses of Deuteronomy 17; and if he neglects to hear them, “tell it unto the church”.

But not everything is a Matthew 18. Matthew 18 goes into severe sin, a matter worthy of putting somebody out of the body, “as an heathen man and a publican”, not a petty disagreement over a parking space, a stepped-on toe, or a mispronounced name. That is the righteous judgment the cities of refuge stood for: a man does not die by a hot heart, he stands before the congregation.

precepts.text: Christ said of the little ones that in heaven their angels do always behold the face of his Father; every one of us that has repented has a guardian angel assigned to minister to us and nudge us in the way the Lord wants our life to go.
precepts.point: Gideon brings a kid and unleavened cakes, and the angel touches the flesh and the cakes with the end of his staff; fire rises up out of the rock and consumes them, and the angel departs out of his sight, gone just like that. No lighter fluid existed on the earth; the angel made fire come out of the rock, because the angels are made out of that fire.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The angel that sat under the oak, received Gideon's offering and vanished is the kind of being that is with us. Christ said of the little ones, “Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.”

Every one of us that has repented has a guardian angel assigned to minister to us and nudge us in the way the Lord wants our life to go. The angel of the Lord ministered to Gideon at the rock in Ophrah; their angels behold the face of the Father in heaven and minister to his little ones now.

precepts.text: Except ye be converted and become as little children ye shall not enter the kingdom, because a child is teachable and will not argue back when it is time to learn.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure because the prophecies in this Bible are sure; we have a more sure word of prophecy. Did we not go into slavery on ships like the Most High declared through Moses in Deuteronomy 28? We are living proof that the Bible is real.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
Christ shows how serious conversion is: “Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

Except ye be converted and become as little children, ye shall not enter the kingdom. Why a little child? A child is teachable and will not argue back when it is time to learn. That is the conversion of the soul that the law of the Lord works in us.

precepts.text: Whosoever shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven; we must humble ourselves as little children.
precepts.point: The testimony of the Lord is sure because the prophecies in this Bible are sure; we have a more sure word of prophecy. Did we not go into slavery on ships like the Most High declared through Moses in Deuteronomy 28? We are living proof that the Bible is real.

note.label: Psalm 19: The Perfect Law That Converts the Soul

precepts.why:
“Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.” Becoming as a little child means humbling yourself, being teachable and not arguing back when it is time to learn.

We must humble ourselves as little children. That is how the law converts the soul, and the one who humbles himself that way is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

precepts.text: Except you be converted and become as little children you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: We have to come back to this Bible as a child. It is not about your age when you come to the truth; that is a carnal thing. A person can be 40 or 50 and sit among people who look younger but are spiritually older because they gained the experience of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 131: The Weaned Child and the Milk of the Word

precepts.why: “Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.” We have to come back to this Bible as a child, the way David quieted himself as a child weaned of his mother. Age is a carnal thing; what counts is being converted and becoming as a little child that desires the milk of the word.

precepts.text: Every one of us has an angel assigned that beholds the Father's face; one way the Lord sees and knows all things is through the angels who write everything down, though the Lord Himself can see all things at any time He chooses.
precepts.point: At the end he asks the Lord to search him, know his heart, try him, and see if there be any wicked way in him and lead him in the way everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 139: The All-Seeing God

precepts.why:
“Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Christ says, “Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.” Every one of us has an angel assigned that beholds the Father’s face.

One way the Lord sees and knows all things is through the angels, who write everything down, though the Lord himself can see all things at any time he chooses. So when David asks to be searched and tried, he knows nothing is hidden, and the same all-seeing God knows the bloody men who speak against him wickedly, the ones David hates with perfect hatred and counts his enemies.

precepts.text: Go and tell thy brother his fault between thee and him alone; if he hears thee, thou hast gained thy brother.
precepts.point: There is a difference in offense. If you offend a brother or cause harm, make it right; but if you bring out God's commandments, such as a sister wearing what belongs to a man or a brother refusing to grow his beard, and they are offended, then they are offended at Christ, not at you.

note.label: Proverbs 18: The Power of the Tongue and Righteous Judgment

precepts.why:
“A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city: and their contentions are like the bars of a castle.” Once you offend someone it is very hard to win them back. So Christ gives the way: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.”

Go straight to the source rather than becoming a talebearer. Tell him his fault between thee and him alone, and if he hears thee, thou hast gained thy brother instead of losing him behind the bars of a castle.

precepts.text: Go and tell your brother his fault between you and him alone; if he hears you, you have gained your brother.
precepts.point: If you reveal the secret, the one who hears it will put you to shame and your bad reputation will not turn away, because now your business is put out there.

note.label: Proverbs 25: The Proverbs of Solomon Copied by Hezekiah's Men

precepts.why:
“Debate thy cause with thy neighbour himself; and discover not a secret to another”. Debating your cause with your neighbor himself means going to him directly.

Christ teaches the same order: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.” Tell him his fault between you and him alone, and if he hears you, you have gained your brother. The matter stays between the two of you.

Go to the neighbor himself, not to a third party. That is how a cause is debated without the secret getting out and shame turning back on you.

precepts.text: There must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.
precepts.point: What is in a man that will not let him go on has to be cut off. Better to enter into life maimed than to keep the thing and be cast into the fire.

note.label: Matthew 18: Offences, the Rule for a Trespassing Brother, and Forgiveness

precepts.why:
“Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” Offences must come. They will come in the congregation, because everyone comes out of a different life and is still learning the others. Much of what offends is small and passes once brethren know each other.

Paul says the same of the congregation: “For there must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you.” There must be heresies, as there must be offences, and there is a purpose in it: they make manifest who is approved. The offences that come show who will go on and who will be turned aside by them.

That is why what is in a man that will not let him go on has to be cut off. If the hand, the foot or the eye offends, cut it off and cast it from you; it is better to enter into life halt or maimed than to keep the thing and be cast into everlasting fire.

precepts.text: "The Son of man is come to save that which was lost," which is the restitution of all things, something lost being recovered.
precepts.point: To fit the other nations into this as the gentiles who are grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. The scriptures show the opposite: the nations are the ones who did the stealing and the hiding, so they are not the gentiles being restored.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
“For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.” That is the restitution of all things: something lost being recovered and given back to its owner.

To fit the other nations into this as gentiles grafted in, you have to prove they lost something or had something stolen from them. Christ came to save what was lost, and the scriptures say who that is.

precepts.text: Their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.
precepts.point: The witness under Christ is not two or three men but the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face, so nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: Acts 5: All Things Common, and We Ought to Obey God Rather Than Men

precepts.why:
“Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.”

The witness under Christ is not two or three men. It is the Most High himself and the angels who always behold his face. Ananias and Sapphira agreed together in private, but nothing is hidden from him.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?” “I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” That is four hundred and ninety times. If he comes and acknowledges what he did wrong and says he is sorry, you have to forgive him. You cannot say, I don’t think he really repented, so I’m not forgiving him. You want a good conscience before God.

But forgiveness and repentance go both ways. A sister tells another sister her personal business in confidence, and she goes gossiping. You rebuke her, she says I’m sorry, and you must forgive her. But would you still tell her your personal business? You would be an idiot. She broke your trust, and she has to win it back. When you hurt somebody and they forgive you, you have to prove yourself to them again and gain back their trust.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” From your hearts, not from your mouth. You can say I forgive you while deep down you are still carrying secret hatred, a grudge for what that person did, and you don’t want to let it go even though they said they were sorry.

To forgive from your heart is to forgive and forget: you don’t hold on to it anymore, you heal from the hurt they did to you. If you don’t forgive from the heart, the Lord will destroy you. And the Lord sees your heart, whether you really forgave that person.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
This is why the Lord shows us how to deal with offences. “Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come”. People will offend each other. Don’t come to this truth thinking nobody will offend you. Leaders offend people too, and when told, say, I’m sorry, I didn’t mean to offend you. The key thing is you can’t hold it inside.

Why must offences come? To prove us, to see if we will apply God’s laws. Offences make everybody stronger and better: when a brother says this offended me, you learn to be more mindful how you deal with certain brothers. But if you are not of the elect, those offences will take you out of the truth: she said this to me, he said that, I ain’t coming back to the school no more. Leaders sit back and watch how brothers and sisters deal with it, and smile when they apply the law, because they are growing. That is how we tell who is approved, who is real in this truth. Offences come to teach us, to make us stronger, and to weed out the fake people among us.

How you deal with the offence decides whether you get the kingdom. Somebody may do evil to you, then go to the Lord and be sorry, while you never forgive, and you don’t get the kingdom.

“But woe to that man by whom the offence cometh! Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee”.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil”.

Charity thinketh no evil. Evil surmising destroys many. Satan talks in your mind, in your ears. But if you are applying the law, love thy neighbour as thyself, which is charity, you will not think evil: probably that brother didn’t mean it like that, probably that sister didn’t mean it like that. And if they did mean it as evil, God knows the heart, and the Lord will deal with it.

Satan always attacks us first in the mind. He plants seeds and thoughts: I don’t think that sister likes you, I don’t think that brother likes you, I don’t think the deacon likes me, why does he be rolling like that? That is where the fight begins, and that is where you have to destroy him, before it manifests in your actions. You literally have to repeat God’s commandments in your head: charity thinketh no evil. That is how you fight.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
“Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more.” To admonish is to warn. The thing you heard, or thought he did, he may not have done. Go to him first. And if he did it, tell him, don’t ever do that again, that’s wrong.

“Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again.” Sometimes the person didn’t say it, or said it but didn’t mean it the way you took it.

“Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.” Many times people are lying: that brother said this about you. Don’t believe everything you hear. Years ago it was said of a brother that he had a Christian spirit on him, and in 2018 a man leaving the truth went and told him, trying to plant evil in his head. But that brother came straight to the deacon and asked, did you say that? Yes, because the way you move is some Christian stuff; you’ve got to man up, be a soldier, be militant-minded. When leaders say things it is never to destroy you, but to make you better. He understood and didn’t carry it. He could have secretly hated, but he came. That is how you can tell who is real: trials have to come.

“There is one that slippeth in his speech, but not from his heart”. Something might come off wrong, but they didn’t mean anything bad in it. “And who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?” Everybody offends with what they say. What matters is how you deal with it: carry secret hatred, a grudge, or go and talk, and they say, damn, I didn’t mean it that way, I’m sorry, and it’s done. Many brothers have left the truth because a root of bitterness sprang up inside them, and bitterness usually comes from offence or correction.

“Admonish thy neighbour before thou threaten him”. Warn him first before you snatch him up by his neck. Find out if he said it or did it before threatening to knock his head off. This is negroes we are talking about. “And not being angry, give place to the law of the most High.” Give place to forgiveness: the brother might repent and say I’m sorry. If you go threatening him, his ego might flare up and you are both going back and forth.

“The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted of him”.

note.label: FORGIVENESS, THE BLOOD COVENANT

precepts.why:
This is why Christ gave this analogy. One “which owed him ten thousand talents”, and “his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.” That is us: we were sold, we went into slavery. The lord is the Lord.

“The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.” He loosed him: that goes into jubilee.

But the same servant found a fellowservant “which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.” Where’s my money? And when his fellowservant begged patience, “he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.”

“O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?” You owed ten million and were forgiven; he owed you a hundred, and you couldn’t show him compassion. We have to be able to forgive each other, forgiving debts as our debts are forgiven.

“And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors”. The tormentors are the angels, the reapers. “So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.” Forgive your brother his trespass.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20

precepts.why: “Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones”: the little ones are those that have repented in Christ. “That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven”: their, possessive. Every one of us has an angel who records what we do and reports to the Father. Esau calls it a guardian angel, and they got that from the Bible. That is rank, order, structure.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why:
We are servants; God's son Jesus was a servant, and if we are following Christ that makes us servants. Some of you think you are almighty; no, brother, you are here to serve, that is your job. Put it perfectly: the deacon is here to make the bishop look good, the captain is here to make the deacons look good, the officers are here to make the captains look good, and so on. That is called unity, that is called leadership, that is called government.

“And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.” Everybody wants to be the chief, nobody wants to be the Indian; everybody wants to be chief but nobody wants to serve. I want the title, but I don't want to live up to the title; I just want to tell men what to do. Brothers, as leaders, if you are not ready to pick up the mop and mop the floor, you should not expect another brother to do it either, because it starts with you. A great leader raises men to be better leaders than himself; do not try to keep the brother down; you are supposed to build that brother up to be better than you; if that brother is not better than you, something is wrong.

A brother said this officer teaches better than this captain, this captain teaches better than the bishop, than the deacon. You are crazy. In Esau's world every one of us went to school to learn from a teacher, a professor. You woke up one day and said I'm better than this professor? You can go on YouTube right now and learn how to do surgery, but you are not going to let me perform on you; the first thing you'll say is, Deacon, what is your qualification, what school did you go to? Take some common sense. If you say the deacon is a good teacher, guess what: the Bishop is better. If my captains are good teachers, I am better than them; if the officers teach better than the captain, no, the captain is better, because they are learning from the higher rank. You think Peter was greater than Christ? You're an idiot. Those are common sense. That is when men start thinking they are beyond themselves: look how I teach. One brother who left said you don't have to watch Deacon so-and-so any more, which one do you want to watch, myself? Where is he at today? Those are foolish thoughts of men who are over themselves, not humbling. This mission is all about humbling, and exalting one another in due time. All those young men remember a few precepts and know how to put them together so the words sound sweet to you, but they don't know what the spirit world requires: the spirit world hates pride; pride and disrespect are not accepted in the spiritual world. Paul said these things are earthly, an earthly doctrine.

And the sister who just came in a year ago and married an officer says I'm an officer's wife and eats before the sister that has been labouring for three, four, five years. Does that make sense? The sister that married the officer of ten is no leader of nothing, but she exalts her power against a sister that lined up for years. What scripture is that? The scripture says let the young women learn from the sisters that were there before them. Hell no; you are not going to pass that. Some congregations say nothing to it: the officer of ten's wife eats and the little sister who has been labouring for years sits in the back. That can hurt somebody's spirit. Everybody has to deserve their name; get your own name, build your own legacy, put your own bricks in; don't ride on my name. Brothers who are leaders: when your wife tries to use your authority to abuse other sisters, hell no, it is not going down like that. Show some respect and honour to those who were there before you. It doesn't matter if she is Deacon so-and-so's wife; she cannot abuse or disrespect you. We are trying to escape looking down upon each other; that is why we are in this captivity in the first place, because we decided not to obey these laws and to live like savages. If you are returning to the Lord you better understand what savage is, what disrespect is, what pride is. We are here to guide you the right way as long as you believe what God said; but you have to be willing to listen and apply it, not only learn precepts.

note.label: Assata & Saddam: a Tale of 2 Revolutions

precepts.why:
What does it mean to be converted? “The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul”. The only thing that can convert your soul is God’s law. That is what your children should be doing and what you sisters should be doing, not playing video games, wasting your life, getting wrong information put in your spirit and your soul.

A story: a couple we knew years ago. At Christmas she bought him a leather coat and he bought her a book, and she cursed him out for it. Then they went to talk, and when he told her sure, in time, we’re working on it, she said that’s not what Jeff said: on the Edge of Night, you’re supposed to respond like that. That’s the mentality of a lot of sisters: if you don’t respond the way the TV guy said, there’s something wrong with you. Your mind is stuck on TV, sis; that’s not reality. Some of your wives want you to act and talk like the TV people do.

They watch Tyler Perry: the dark one is always the bad guy, the evil one, and you need a light-skinned brother to come save the woman: ‘get away from her, Blackie.’ All his movies are like that, and that’s why she says she wants a light-skinned brother. That’s colorism. So it’s good to change, but the soul gets converted by God’s law.

note.label: Assata & Saddam: a Tale of 2 Revolutions

precepts.why:
This goes with Matthew 18:3, where Christ said except you be converted as a little child you cannot enter the kingdom of heaven on earth. “Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding”: everything you learned from the age of five to the age you are now, forget about it. Subdue it, push it down, don’t meditate on it, get it out the way.

“And reform your hearts”: reform means change, transform; heart means mind. Transform your mind. “Ye shall be kept alive”: kept alive for the coming kingdom. “And after death ye shall obtain mercy”: after this body dies you shall obtain mercy, you’re going to get eternal life. That’s what the angel was telling Ezra.

note.label: Assata & Saddam: a Tale of 2 Revolutions

precepts.why:
It’s about changing your mind. “Have put on the new man, which is renewed in knowledge after the image of him that created him”. Start at verse eight: “But now ye also put off all these; anger”: we got to put that away. Wrath, “malice”: put that away. “Blasphemy”: put that away. “Filthy communication out of your mouth”: put that away, and yes, that includes twerking. “Lie not one to another”: we can’t do it.

“Seeing that ye have put off the old man with his deeds”. Our job, brothers and sisters, is to be transformed to the image of Christ, to follow the pattern of Christ to the best of our ability. There’s no such thing as a brother or a sister with a bad attitude and we say, oh, that’s just him, that’s just her. No, our job is to be changed into the image of Christ. You can’t stay an alcoholic: if you was an alcoholic, stop drinking. You cursing everybody out as soon as somebody tries to have a decent conversation: stop that.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Breakdown Of Revelation 16

precepts.why: “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.” The point of the whole thing is to gain your brother, to win him back. But one said, my point is not to gain you, my point is to entrap you in your words and make a video to embarrass you. Those are elements of Satan. When they can’t touch who you have become, they dig up your past.

note.label: ​ | Sabbath Evening Class: Secrets in the Lord's Prayer

precepts.why:
Let me give it to you. “Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.” Whoa, that’s hard for black people, Latino people to do.

“Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants.” One owed him “ten thousand talents”, of silver, but this servant didn’t have nothing to pay, so “his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had”: sell his wife, sell his snotty-nosed kids, even the house he got, and payment to be made. The servant fell down and worshipped him, begging, please have mercy on me, I’ll pay you all back. “Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.” That last word, debt: Christ is talking about sins. He forgave all of us the debts we owe.

“But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.” Now this is some of you. The same thing happens in reverse: have mercy on me, I’ll pay you all. “And he would not”: this is some of us in here, some of us listening. No, I’m not forgiving you. He threw him in jail till he should pay the debt.

Back in 2018 there were a lot of problems in Austin, Texas, and on false charges they had a man thrown in jail. ‘I’m sorry, brother, I’ll make it right’, and they said no, we want you in jail. This is what we’re reading about. Some of them just set up a church and try to ignore all the evil they did. Now they say, brother, I apologize, sister, I apologize, and that’s not good enough. They cast the brother into prison under false pretenses.

“O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?” The Lord is saying, I had compassion on you; shouldn’t y’all have had compassion on him? “And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him. So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.”

You see how heavy that thing is. The same grace the Lord gave to you, you’re supposed to give to that man. You had the chance to go back and fix what you messed up, but you have not fixed it; you built a church upon sin, and you’re hoping people respect you, hoping people have mercy upon you. The same things you did are coming back to you: be very mindful how you’re operating the spirit. Extra mercy was given to you; why not extra mercy to that man, him and his family? Now the things Christ died for are all on you. Your sin remains.

That goes with ‘there must be offenses, but woe be unto that man by whom the offense cometh’. There are offenses that were done and never corrected, and the Most High has that written down.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 10 The Little Book, Sweet and Bitter

precepts.why: How is it bitter to us as an individual? “For it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” “Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee”: your hand or foot is somebody very close to you. People ask why we cut people off; because they are an offence to this truth, and we are commanded to, however much we love them. “It is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed”: better to cast them away than for all of you to be cast into destruction.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 15 The Seven Last Plagues

precepts.why:
“Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone”: if I got a problem with a brother, should I go to someone else about it? No. The Bible says you go to your brother, you go to your sister. But instead, people go on Facebook, they go on YouTube, evil as hell.

Why did Christ have to put that in the Bible? Why did the Son of God have to make it a law? Because we still have that same spirit Christ was trying to stop back then. It should be basic common knowledge, but he knew it was going to happen, so he had it written and documented.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
What converts us to becoming little children? “The law of the Lord is perfect”. Brothers and sisters, especially you men on the street, don’t get hemmed up with these stupid people that find a number in Kings, like how many horses were in Solomon’s barn, and a different number in Chronicles, or a king’s age when he began to rule in Kings and a different one in Chronicles, and say, see, imperfection, these are typos. Don’t argue about typos: oh look, Noah is spelled N-O-E over here but N-O-A-H in Genesis. Why are you arguing about that? That’s stupid.

There’s no problems with God’s law. When God says thou shalt not commit adultery, that’s perfection. When he says thou shalt not kill, that’s perfection. When he says thou shalt not bear false witness, that is perfection.

In an interview in South Africa a man asked whether the writings in the Bible are 100 percent accurate. That was a trap, so the answer was: there are some words that shouldn’t be there, like the word Easter in Acts 12. That’s a pagan term; the Israelites never celebrated that, and when you examine it the word Passover was there initially. Easter goes back to Ishtar, Esther’s name, which goes back to Ashtaroth in the book of Kings: holidays of the fertility goddess, sexuality, babies and abortions. Read from verse one through three and it tells you we were celebrating the feast of unleavened bread. Always be prepared for these people that try to hem you up.

“Converting the soul”: the law is what converts us. “The testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We got to acknowledge we’re the simple. Brother, I don’t care what kind of degree you got, you are simple. Sister, we’re the most educated generation, simple as hell. If you want to be wise you got to go to the perfection of the Lord, which is his law. Masters, doctorate or whatever, you’re simple until you come back to God’s laws.

note.label: Rise Of An Unseen Government

precepts.why: “Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?” Christ answered, “Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” If you will enter into life, do what? Keep the commandments. Y’all understand that, brothers and sisters: he said keep the commandments.

note.label: Rise Of An Unseen Government

precepts.why: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.” Christ said if you love me, keep my commandments. That’s what he said.

precepts.why: “And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.” If they don’t want to hear the congregation, let them be as heathens and publicans; and Israel did not deal with the heathens and publicans. note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 2

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 14 Part 2

precepts.why: People speak great words and you follow after the great words, but that is not what the scripture says. “Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone”. The scripture says you and him alone; a recorder makes a third. So that man has not followed the Lamb wherever he goes: these are not the elect.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
This is a big one. “Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” Notice what Christ said: offences will come. You men and women come into this truth, and sisters always ask, if I come to IUIC, are all the sisters nice? No, they are not; they are struggling with sin just like you. You come here thinking it is a bed of roses; it ain't like that. When the scriptures say love your neighbour as you love yourself, you all say you obey that. How could you say you obey it unless it has been tested? It can only be tested in the congregation; you have to come around other brothers and sisters to test that theory you hold dear. Then you find out and say, I'm out of here, because I don't like brother so-and-so, I don't like sister so-and-so, they offended me over something small. Like all of you that said, I'm leaving because of the Bishop, I'm out of here. A whole slew of you rats, traitor bastards, ran out of here, turncoats. Shame on you. You love your neighbour as you love yourself? The devil is a liar, and you have been proven a liar. Not you, I know you've done no wrong.

“Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.” They say, oh, but he did this and he was put out for a year, and now he wants to repent. points: You can’t enter the kingdom except you be converted and become like a child: start all over again. “Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child”: humble himself to God’s laws. “The same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.” You want to be great? Humble yourself to God’s laws.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.” If you accept one of them that believes in Christ, you receive Christ.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “But whoso shall offend one of these little ones”: trying to get you to sin, trying to get you to break God’s law, “which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.” Christ is saying it’s better that you kill yourself. That goes back to the scripture that says, how you gonna love God and hate the brother who is in front of you? You offend one of these brothers that believe in Christ, you got a price to pay for that.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!” For it must needs be that offenses come: we’re going to touch on why they need to come in a little bit.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee”: that hand or foot is symbolic for your friend, family or neighbor. “Cut them off, and cast them from thee”. It’s better to enter into the kingdom without your friend, without your wife, without your husband, without your child, “rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.” Remember the hell we read about earlier in Matthew 5: that hell is this part here, everlasting fire.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “And if thine eye offend thee”: the eye is your mama, your daddy, your sister or brother. “Pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.” Hell fire: Moses spoke about the same thing.

I don’t care if you’re 70 years old or 80. Moses was 80 years old when God called him, so age is no excuse; you just rebellious. Abraham was around 100 years old. If they can be that old and change, you mean your old stank self can’t change at 65 or 75? What the hell is wrong with you? You got a few years left; you better change. Become like this little child: forget all that garbage you learned.

“Ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven”: you can’t enter the kingdom of heaven unless you start all over again as a child in this truth. If you’ve been in this truth one year, you are a one-year-old child; eight years, an eight-year-old child; twelve years, a twelve-year-old child. Some brothers and sisters say, I’m grown, you don’t tell me what to do. You ain’t got that little child spirit; you got that old spirit on you.
